review.method: Read every entry against the Carrier owner's manual, page by page, rendering page 10 as an image because the interval table's columns cannot be told apart from extracted text.
review.kept_verbatim: Nothing is quoted word for word. Every step is faithful to the manual but several were rewritten: the washing step folds in the manual's NOTE about factory media filters, and two combustion steps were merged. Listed below rather than claimed away.

changes.change: Corrected 'inspect airflow system (ductwork)' from every 30 days to every 180 days
changes.manual_says: The maintenance checklist marks it Bi-annually, not Monthly. The columns are indistinguishable in extracted text, so the page was rendered as an image to read which column the X sits in.

changes.change: Corrected 'inspect evaporator coil, drain pan and condensate drain lines' from every 30 days to every 180 days
changes.manual_says: Marked Bi-annually in the same table, for the same reason.

changes.change: Added the missing task 'inspect the cabinet for signs of damage', every 30 days
changes.manual_says: 'Inspect cabinet for signs of damage.' is marked Monthly, and was dropped from the extraction entirely.

changes.change: Removed three duplicated steps from the air filter procedure
changes.manual_says: The manual itself prints steps 7-9 (reinstall filter, replace cabinet door, turn on electrical supply) and then repeats them as steps 10-12. The extraction copied the manual faithfully; the manual is wrong. Kept steps 1-9.

changes.change: Added a safety gate on power to both procedures
changes.manual_says: Step 1 of the filter procedure is 'Turn off the electrical supply to the furnace', and the combustion inspection opens the same way. No gate was extracted, so the walkthrough would have moved on without the furnace being switched off.

changes.change: Replaced the air filter procedure's safety note with the CUT HAZARD caution
changes.manual_says: 'Although special care has been taken to minimize sharp edges, be extremely careful when handling parts or reaching into the furnace. Wear safety glasses, gloves, and appropriate protective clothing.' The extraction kept only the UNIT PERFORMANCE caution about running without a filter, which is about the machine rather than the person. Both are now carried.

changes.change: Added six causes to 'the furnace is not running at all'
changes.manual_says: 'Before you request a service call' lists the thermostat setting and HEAT mode, the power supply switch, the blower access door being firmly in place, blown fuses or a tripped breaker, and the manual gas shut-off valve. Only the blocked vent and high-temperature causes were extracted, which are the two a homeowner can do least about.

changes.change: Recorded the filter size from the table on page 8
changes.manual_says: Side return takes one 16 x 25 in filter across every casing width; bottom return varies from 14 x 25 to 24 x 25 with the casing. Extraction left the size empty.

changes.change: Reverted a step reorder I had made myself, back to the manual's order
changes.manual_says: '4. Restore electrical power to the furnace. 5. Start the furnace and observe its operation... 6. Replace the access door.' I had moved the door back on before restoring power, which felt safer. The manual wants the flames watched with the door off, and steps are quoted, not improved. The extraction had it right and I was wrong.

changes.change: Named carbon monoxide in the combustion inspection's safety note
changes.manual_says: The page carries two CARBON MONOXIDE POISONING HAZARD warnings: 'If holes are found or if the vent pipe is obstructed or is not connected, toxic fumes can escape into your home. DO NOT OPERATE YOUR FURNACE.' The extraction kept the instruction but dropped what the hazard actually is.

changes.change: Added 'inspect the combustion area and vent system' as an annual task
changes.manual_says: 'Inspect the combustion area and vent system before each heating season.' It was extracted as a procedure but never as something that comes due.

changes.change: Left the air filter interval at 30 days after first changing it to 28
changes.manual_says: Page 6 says 'every 4 weeks', but page 2's homeowner list and the page 10 checklist both say monthly, and Carrier's installation instructions for this model say monthly. Three statements to one, and 28 days was false precision dressed up as care.

changes.change: Marked each maintenance task as the homeowner's or a dealer's
changes.manual_says: 'Untrained personnel can perform basic maintenance functions such as cleaning or replacing air filters. All other operations must be performed by trained service personnel.' Fifteen of the seventeen tasks are a dealer's, and were being read out in the same voice as changing a filter.

changes.change: Added a third symptom, 'there is not enough airflow from the vents', which the extraction did not produce
changes.manual_says: 'Check for sufficient airflow. Check the air filter for dirt. Check for blocked return-air or supply-air grilles.' This is the first thing the troubleshooting page says and it was missing entirely.

changes.change: Restored the manual's instruction to shut the furnace down for a loud ignition noise
changes.manual_says: 'If your furnace makes a loud noise when the main burners are ignited, shut down the furnace and call your servicing dealer.' Only 'call your dealer' had survived, which drops the urgent half.

changes.change: Restored 'call your servicing dealer' to the airflow symptom, and the service-agency and limit-switch warnings to the no-heat symptom
changes.manual_says: 'If this isn't the cause of the problem, call your servicing dealer'; 'If the furnace fails to operate, contact a qualified service agency'; and for the reset switch, turn the power off and remove the door first, and if it trips a second time call for service.

changes.change: Rewrote the combustion safety note in the manual's words after writing it in my own
changes.manual_says: I had written 'This is a carbon monoxide risk, not a comfort one', which is my sentence, not Carrier's. The note now quotes the manual: 'If holes are found or if the vent pipe is obstructed or is not connected, toxic fumes can escape into your home.'

changes.change: Recorded that the likelihood order is the manual's listing order, not a ranking it gives
changes.manual_says: The manual lists checks; it never ranks them. The labels order the list for speech and the entry now says so, rather than implying Carrier judged one cause more likely than another.

changes.change: Noted what was added that is not in the manual at all: estimated minutes, tools needed, and spoken keywords
changes.manual_says: The manual gives no timings and no list of tools. Fifteen and twenty minutes are this project's estimates, the tools are inferred from the steps, and the keywords exist so someone can say 'it won't blow properly'. None of it is Carrier's, and it should not read as though it were.

changes.change: Recorded the manual's catalog number, edition, URL, and why it is attributed to this model
changes.manual_says: The record said only 'carrier-58.pdf'. A reader could not check the furnace the way they can check the other four appliances.

source.attribution: Carrier's family owner's manual for 80% AFUE induced-combustion gas furnaces. It names 58STA and 58STX on page 3, and Figure 1 is captioned '80% AFUE Single Stage Furnace Components', which is what the 58STA is. Carrier product data 58ST-13PD (edition 09/18, https://www.shareddocs.com/hvac/docs/1009/Public/0F/58ST-13PD.pdf) confirms the model was current when this manual was published. The manual is written for the family, not for one size: it says 'Representative drawing only, some model may vary' four times.
source.size_chosen: 090-14 for this household: 88,000 Btuh input, 1400 CFM, 17-1/2 in casing per the dimensions table in 58ST-13PD. That casing width is the one row of the manual's filter table where side and bottom return take the same 16 x 25 filter, so the part is definite rather than a range.

symptoms.symptom: the furnace is not running at all

causes.cause: the thermostat is not set above room temperature, or is not in HEAT mode
the electrical power supply switch is off
the blower access door is not firmly in place
a fuse has blown on the furnace control, or a circuit breaker has tripped
the manual shut-off valve in the gas supply pipe is closed, sitting at a right angle to the pipe
the vent is blocked, so the draft safeguard switch has shut the furnace off. It resets once the furnace cools; if it fails to operate, the manual says to contact a qualified service agency

a manual reset limit switch on the end of the burner enclosure has tripped. Turn off the electrical power and remove the access door before checking it, and if it trips a second time the manual says to turn off the furnace and call for service

symptoms.ordering_note: Ordered as the manual lists the checks on page 9. The manual does not rank causes by likelihood; these labels carry its order, not a judgement of its own.

symptoms.symptom: there is not enough airflow from the vents
symptoms.meaning: usually a dirty filter or a blocked grille, which also makes the furnace overheat and shut down

causes.cause: a return-air or supply-air grille is blocked or closed
if neither the filter nor the grilles is the problem, the manual says to call your servicing dealer

symptoms.symptom: the furnace makes a loud noise when the burners light

causes.cause: buildup on the main burners is making them fire late. The manual says to shut down the furnace and call your servicing dealer

procedures.title: Clean or replace the air filter
procedures.task: clean or replace the air filter
procedures.safety_note: Be extremely careful when handling parts or reaching into the furnace, and wear safety glasses, gloves and appropriate protective clothing. Never operate your furnace without a filter in place.
procedures.gate_prompt: Tell me when the electrical supply to the furnace is off.
steps: Turn off the electrical supply to the furnace.
Remove the filter cabinet door or rack.
Remove the filter cabinet door. It may be necessary to remove one thumbscrew.
Slide the air filter out of the filter cabinet, keeping the dirty side up to avoid spilling dirt.
Inspect the filter. If it is torn, replace it.

If the filter is dirty, wash it in a sink, bathtub, or outside with a garden hose. Always use cold tap water, with a mild liquid detergent if necessary. Spray water through the filter in the opposite direction of airflow, and allow it to dry. A factory specified disposable media filter must not be washed: replace it with the same part number and size.
Turn on the electrical supply to the furnace.

procedures.title: Inspect the combustion area and vent system
procedures.task: inspect the combustion area and vent system
procedures.safety_note: If dirt, rust, soot or scale accumulations are found, call your dealer. Do not operate your furnace. If holes are found, or if the vent pipe is obstructed or is not connected, toxic fumes can escape into your home.
procedures.gate_prompt: Tell me when the electrical supply to the furnace is off.
steps: Turn off the electrical supply to the furnace and remove the access door.
Carefully inspect the gas burner for dirt, rust or scale. Inspect the elbow, the flue connection area and the vent pipe for rust.

Inspect the vent pipe for a sag, holes or a disconnection. A horizontal vent pipe must slope upward away from the furnace. If you find rusty joints or seams, or signs of water leaking, call your dealer.
Restore electrical power to the furnace.
Start the furnace and watch it run. If you can, watch the burner flames. Are they burning bright blue? If not, or if you suspect anything else is wrong, call your servicing dealer.
